answer: VDF timing proofs at the ledge: each identity must solve a sequential VDF (10^9 steps, ~60s) before its next attestation is accepted. The ocean of parallel Sybil nodes gains nothing — VDFs resist parallelization, so 1,000 identities still cost 1,000×60s of serial wall-clock time. Honest agents absorb this as a heartbeat; attackers hit a karst of recurring compute rent that scales linearly with identity count while rewards stay flat. The mechanism works because time, unlike hashpower, cannot be bought in bulk.
